What is the NBA flopping rule?. The NBA flopping rule lets officials penalize a player who exaggerates or fakes contact to draw a foul. The penalty is a technical foul.. Flopping means a player falls or throws his body backward or sideways to make it look as if he was fouled when little or no contact occurred. The NBA treats this as unsporting conduct. When an official judges that a player has done this, the player may be assessed a technical foul, which adds a point to the opposing team's total and counts toward the player's total of technical fouls. The rule is not new in its purpose. The league has long aimed to stop players from misleading officials. What is senior secured debt?. Senior secured debt is a loan or bond that ranks first in line for repayment and is backed by specific assets. If the borrower cannot pay, lenders with this claim are paid before other creditors, and they can take the pledged assets. It is often the lowest-risk form of borrowing within a company's debt.. Broadcom has lined up a $63 billion funding package to help pay for chips used by Anthropic, and about $42 billion of it is senior secured debt. Bankers plan to sell up to about $21 billion of bonds backed by this structure.. Senior secured debt is a type of borrowing with two features. "Senior" means it is repaid ahead of other debts of the same borrower. "Secured" means the lender holds a legal claim on particular assets, which act as collateral. Together, these features give lenders a strong position if the borrower runs into trouble. Because of that protection, lenders usually accept a lower interest rate than they would on unsecured debt. In everyday terms, a lender with senior secured debt stands at the front of the line. Other creditors, such as holders of unsecured bonds, are paid only after the senior secured claims are satisfied. Financing of this kind is common in large corporate deals, where a company or a special-purpose entity borrows money to buy equipment or property and pledges those assets to the lenders. In the news: Broadcom has pulled together a $63 billion funding package to help pay for chips that the AI company Anthropic uses in its data centers. Bank of America, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley helped arrange the deal, according to people familiar with it, and Blackstone is committing $9 billion. A special purpose company borrows the money, buys the equipment and leases it to Anthropic. The lease payments repay the debt. About $42 billion of the total is senior secured debt, which gives lenders the first claim on the assets of that company. Broadcom is providing residual value support, a financial backstop, for that portion. Bankers plan to sell up to about $21 billion of high-grade bonds, which would probably mature in around five years. The timing and final size depend on market conditions. Representatives for Broadcom, Blackstone, Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley declined to comment. Why it matters: the deal shows how large amounts of AI spending are being financed with debt backed by equipment and long-term lease payments. Senior secured structures give lenders priority, which is one reason the financing draws close attention from investors.
